C_MEDIA_BROWSER_CANDIDATE.required_before_run: Add the named candidate-only Playwright config and source-owned case producer, then amend this placeholder command to pass the sealed candidate identity, sealed run plan, private actor state, and no-replace output root explicitly. They must attach to the existing non-443 candidate, must not start the mock-only Framerail fixture, and must record separate DOMContentLoaded-immediate and settled artifacts with network, console, page-error, CSP-header, CSP-violation, focus, and cleanup observations.

candidate_harness_gap.reason: No existing source-owned candidate runner covers file upload state, WWS bytes, media network policy, and every initial/settled browser interval in one identity-bound receipt.
must_not_substitute: the mock-only default Framerail Playwright fixture
a successful HTTP status without blob and actor identity

reusable_source.reuse: Validate a sealed, fresh, non-standing production candidate identity and its immutable image, source, FTML, configuration, endpoint, and evidence bindings.
Observe every declared candidate service before and after capture and reject container, image, label, health, mount, network, port, or effective-configuration drift.
Reuse candidate attachment, clean-source execution identity, request gating, pre/post runtime stability, and sealed terminal receipt patterns without reusing the fixed standing-canary case set.
Reuse the distinct DOMContentLoaded-immediate and settled capture ordering, resource completion, request-failure collection, and screenshot artifact identities.
Reuse the isolated browser context, non-standing local endpoint, request gate, proxy, service-worker block, and close-all-resources behavior.
Publish terminal plan, case, cleanup, and verdict artifacts without replacing an earlier candidate result.

do_not_reuse_as_acceptance.reason: It starts a mock XML-RPC fixture and a development Framerail preview instead of attaching to the sealed production candidate.
It may coordinate disposable stages, but its mutable state and summary files are not a no-replace terminal acceptance receipt and its generic command plan does not prove media behavior.

missing_contracts.reason: No source-owned fixture plan creates and independently freezes the exact candidate URLs, page and revision identities, file names, expected byte hashes, icon values, media sources, gallery rows, and actor permissions for the ten candidate_required case IDs. A private manifest cannot supply both the observation and its expected value.

The sealed standing candidate identity binds images and effective service configuration, including mount configuration, but it does not identify the contents of the task-owned database and files fixtures. The final plan needs independently sealed DB and files identities plus an allowed run-owned mutation delta.

No secret-free source contract identifies the anonymous, authorized editor, and forbidden actor rows or binds a private browser storage-state file by hash. Credentials must remain outside receipts while actor IDs and permissions remain auditable.

No source-owned executor currently drives the public Framerail, Deepwell, and WWS seams for local icon bytes, upload-delete-rename-revision next reads, multipart serialization, upload transaction order, exact download bytes, and fail-closed route absence. Direct DB access is permitted only for fixture setup and supplemental cleanup/identity assertions, not as the pass oracle.

The candidate-only Playwright config and test do not exist. The standing canary runner captures fixed read-only pages and cannot substitute for icon transitions, media frames, Gallery viewer actions, or multipart upload workflows.

The reusable standing observation records request failures and HTTP error responses, but the media contract also requires console errors, page errors, the main response CSP header, securitypolicyviolation events, iframe request attempts, and fail-closed no-request intervals. These fields need a source-owned media observation contract rather than an assumed empty array.

No creation ledger and finally/signal cleanup executor records ownership of candidate-created pages, revisions, files, pending blobs, and settings, then proves their absence after success or failure. The controller must never stop, remove, or recreate the externally owned candidate stack, DB, cache, or files volumes.

No terminal verifier currently reconciles every candidate_required case exactly once against one sealed plan and the same pre/post runtime identity, rejects skipped or self-reported cases, and publishes case receipts plus the aggregate verdict through the existing no-replace primitive.

The browser case requires an observed before/after icon-setting change, while M756_UPLOAD_MATERIALIZATION remains blocked_evidence for upload/download transaction, replacement, deletion, MIME, size, SVG/script, and failure semantics. The harness must not invent a mutation solely to make the browser row executable.

required_ownership_boundary.candidate_stack: external owner named by the sealed candidate identity; harness observes but does not build, start, stop, replace, or remove it
required_ownership_boundary.run_owned_state: source-owned case producer; every created page, revision, setting delta, file, and pending blob is recorded before use and removed or restored in finally and signal paths
required_ownership_boundary.terminal_evidence: media candidate harness; no-replace publication only after case reconciliation, cleanup absence, and stable post-run candidate observation
required_ownership_boundary.secrets: private operator inputs only; receipts contain actor and storage-state hashes but no credentials, session cookies, presigned URLs, or tokens

review.readiness_rule: Keep both target commands exists_now=false until the named source/config/test files exist, source-blind unit and CLI tests cover every missing contract, and one black-box candidate run proves all ten candidate_required rows without skips. A verifier that only accepts producer-authored pass receipts is not sufficient.

issues.title: Page file upload fails before blob commit

subrows.acceptance: Return successful and failed multipart actions without an arbitrary File object in SvelteKit's serialized payload.
subrows.reason: Source now returns withFiles({ form, res }), which addresses the historical cause, but no current test drives the real action through SvelteKit serialization.

subrows.acceptance: Check Page:Edit, then blob_upload, presigned PUT, and file_create in order, and expose the created file only after relation commit.
subrows.reason: The source order is present and presigned HTTP errors are covered, but only one exact task-owned DB/files candidate can prove the transaction and next read.

subrows.acceptance: Require parent-page edit permission and exact site/page/blob ownership; reject client authority over another pending blob.
subrows.reason: blob_upload now derives page ownership from the trusted request context, the database enforces scoped-or-unscoped shape, and typed page finalization rejects another actor, page, site, or unscoped pending blob without exposing whether the token exists. The public endpoint case proves the successful file_create response and subsequent page_get_files/file_get bytes, with direct database access limited to supplemental ownership-persistence, fixture-setup, and cleanup assertions.
existing_tests: install/local/wikidot-verification/tests/corpus-import-attachments.test.mjs::materializeCorpusRowAttachments binds pending uploads to the trusted page context

subrows.acceptance: On presign, PUT, timeout, or file_create failure, create no file relation, leave no public route, cancel pending state, and preserve list/cache state.
subrows.reason: Every page-scoped upload caller now owns the same failure boundary: the Framerail form flow and XML-RPC bridge share a pending upload lifecycle, while the corpus importer applies the same sequence at its process boundary. After pending allocation, PUT, file_create, or file_edit failure triggers exactly one separate blob_cancel request with the original actor, site, and page context; cleanup failure is suppressed so the original failure remains authoritative, and successful commits are not cancelled. Focused Node cases prove order, context, exactly-once cleanup, original-error preservation, and success behavior. The XML-RPC fixture independently requires exact page-scoped params plus session/site/page headers. The Deepwell public ownership case proves failed commits expose no file relation and now guarantees global pending-row and DB/S3 fixture cleanup after an assertion or teardown panic; direct DB/S3 access remains test-only setup and cleanup. A task-owned runtime candidate still must prove transport timeout, cache, and object-store behavior.
